name: Wave Terminal
tagline: Electron terminal with blocks, widgets, AI and a wsh control CLI

license.notes: Apache-2.0. Wave AI includes free beta credits through Wave's service; BYOK and local models supported.

backing: Command Line Inc. (company, founded 2023 per Slashdot listing; funding not verified)

adoption.summary: Popular open-source desktop terminal (22.5k stars); distributed via its site, Snapcraft and package managers; no public download counts found.

maintainability.release_cadence: Roughly monthly through 2025 to v0.14.5 (2026-04-16); no stable release in the ~6 months since
maintainability.contributors: ~49 (GitHub contributors API with anon, last page index)
maintainability.summary: Steady development by a small company; release cadence has slowed in 2026.

architecture.summary: An Electron app whose window is a tiled layout of 'blocks': terminals, web views, editors, file previews, sysinfo graphs, Wave AI chat and custom widgets defined in widgets.json. A Go backend (wavesrv) holds the object model (workspaces, tabs, blocks with metadata) and exposes RPC; the `wsh` CLI, available inside every Wave terminal including over SSH, talks to it to open views, edit files, set/get block metadata, read terminal scrollback, run commands in new blocks, set badges and list blocks as JSON. Wave AI has internal tools to read terminal output, screenshot widgets, read/write files with approval and navigate web widgets. A Go reactive widget framework, Tsunami (vdom-based, with an AI 'builder'), has been in progress since 2025 ('WaveApps builder framework, not yet released' per release notes).
key_points: Blocks are addressable objects with ids and JSON metadata (wsh getmeta/setmeta)

wsh commands: view, edit, editor, getmeta, setmeta, ai, editconfig, setbg, badge, run, deleteblock, ssh, wsl, web, notify, conn, setconfig, file, launch, getvar/setvar, termscrollback, wavepath, blocks, secret
`wsh blocks list --json` filters by workspace/window/tab/view type
`wsh badge` marketed for Claude Code hooks to surface notifications on blocks
Wave AI tools: read terminal output, capture widget screenshots, read/list/write files (approval), navigate web widgets
Durable SSH sessions (v0.14) survive disconnects and restarts
Tsunami/WaveApps: Go vdom widget framework, unreleased

agent_usability.how: An agent running in a Wave terminal shells out to `wsh` (open a web/preview/editor block, run a command in a new block, set block metadata, read scrollback, list blocks as JSON, badge/notify). Wave's own AI uses internal tools. No MCP server for Wave itself was found.
agent_usability.integration_effort: Zero for CLI agents running inside Wave (wsh is on PATH); nothing for agents outside Wave.
agent_usability.readback: Text scrollback via `wsh termscrollback`, block lists/metadata as JSON; widget screenshots only available to Wave AI internally.
agent_usability.granular_edits: Block-level: setmeta by block id, deleteblock, open/replace views. No patching of UI inside a widget.
agent_usability.history: None for UI/layout; durable SSH sessions preserve shell state.
agent_usability.summary: Agent-drivable at the workspace layout level through a CLI: an agent can open panes and point them at things, but cannot build or patch a custom UI inside them (until Tsunami ships).

score_notes.ui_as_data: block metadata and widgets.json are JSON; widget internals are React code
score_notes.agent_drivable: wsh CLI covers open/run/close/setmeta of blocks for any in-terminal agent
score_notes.readback: scrollback text and block JSON; screenshots only for built-in AI
score_notes.granular_edits: id-addressed block metadata edits, not UI internals
score_notes.live_data_rate: sysinfo graphs and terminals stream; no published rates
score_notes.terminal_native: it is a terminal emulator, but its rich widgets are Electron/web, not terminal cells
score_notes.maturity: 22k stars, years of releases; pre-1.0 versioning

steelman: Wave already gives a coding agent what claude-canvas only demoed: a real second screen with many panes, driven from the command line the agent already lives in. Any CLI agent inside Wave can open a web page, a markdown preview, an image or an editor beside itself, run a command in its own block, badge a block when it needs attention, and read terminal scrollback, all through `wsh`, which works over SSH too. Blocks are addressable objects with JSON metadata, the built-in AI can screenshot widgets and act with approvals, and durable SSH sessions survive restarts. For 'an agent should be able to show me things next to the terminal', Wave is a shipping, Apache-licensed, 22k-star answer.
weaknesses: Electron desktop app, not a terminal-native UI; you must switch terminals to use it
Agent control is coarse (blocks and URLs), with no API to build or patch widget UIs; Tsunami/WaveApps still unreleased
No MCP server for external agents; wsh only works inside Wave terminals
Widget screenshots and AI tools are internal to Wave AI
No history/time travel of UI state

relation_to_scene.overlap: Agent opens and arranges panes beside the terminal and reads terminal text back; block ids with JSON metadata.
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: If the need is only 'show a web page / file / image next to the agent', Wave's blocks already do it. Scene's value is the custom live UI inside a pane, which Wave lacks today.
borrow: A small CLI (`wsh`-style) that works from any shell, including over SSH, as the agent's control surface alongside the socket/MCP
Badges/notify on panes for agent attention (Claude Code hooks)
`blocks list --json` style discovery of live scene instances and their ids
getmeta/setmeta as a generic id-addressed property patch
relation_to_scene.gap_left: Wave cannot render an agent-authored, data-bound, keyboard-driven UI in a pane, read it back as structure, patch it by node id, or rewind it; scene can, and runs in any terminal rather than requiring one desktop app.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: Wave is a host for panes; scene could run inside a Wave terminal block, while Wave's CLI ergonomics are worth copying.
